desk.headline: Profit flat at S/457m as El Niño provisions bite; about 17% ROE target for 2026 kept

other.label: Net profit excl. El Niño provisions

results: Profit was S/457m, flat on a year ago but down 22% from Q2, after Interbank set aside S/185m for a possible strong El Niño; excluding that, profit would have been about S/544m.
Net interest income rose 4.9% and Interbank's margin widened to 5.1% from 4.9% in Q2 as funding costs fell to 2.9%.
Interbank's performing loans grew 9.9% y/y, led by credit cards and personal loans (+18%) and small businesses (+34%); bad loans eased to 2.0% of the book.
Insurer Interseguro earned S/97m, up from S/38m when it booked investment write-downs; wealth arm Inteligo fell to S/38m on weaker portfolio gains.
Interbank's core capital ratio slipped to 11.6% from 11.9% in Q2 as lending grew and the group bought back shares.

guidance.summary: The results release gives no numeric outlook. On the call, management kept its 2026 goals of about 17% ROE and high single-digit loan growth, and raised its medium-term ROE target to above 20%.

points: The El Niño provision followed Peru's forecasters raising the chance of an extraordinary event in Q1 2027 to 55% from 9% in June.
About 11% of loans are potentially exposed, mostly farming and fishing clients seen as low risk; no further El Niño provisions are planned in Q4 for now.
Management expects the interest margin to keep widening but gave no specific figure.
The earlier buyback of about $200m is complete; a new programme is under review with no decision yet.
Management trimmed its Peru growth forecast to 3.2% for 2026 and 3% for 2027, with a weaker first half of 2027.
call.source: Call coverage: Intercorp Financial (IFS) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript — The Motley Fool, 10 Nov 2026

watch: Whether El Niño strikes in early 2027 and if more provisions are needed.
Cost of risk, which ran at 1.9% before the El Niño charge.
A decision on a new share buyback and capital ratios under new rules from December 2026.
